blog-cost-per-outcome: Stop measuring tokens. Measure cost per outcome.
Token pricing is a trap for planning. It tells you what a request cost, not whether it was worth it. The number that actually runs your business is
: what you paid to resolve a ticket, qualify a lead, or book a meeting.
Pick a cheap model and you’ll fumble the hard cases that matter most. Pick an expensive one and you’ll pay reasoning-model prices to answer “what are your opening hours?” Neither is a strategy.
When a fast model handles the routine 80% and a reasoning model takes the tricky 20%, your
cost per outcome drops sharply while quality on the hard cases goes up. A rough shape we see often:
Fast model, routine reply: fractions of a cent.
Reasoning model, complex case: 10–20× more — but rare.
Blended cost per resolved conversation: closer to the cheap end than the expensive one.
Optimise the blend, not the model.
